residentHome: Spielzeugkiste als Ring, Pappschilder an den Seilen
structure: resident monologue in the toy box: the figure swaps heads and each head is a card cutting its own promo; the card-art animals of the toy box are the rest of the roster; ends on the jobber's only choice
synopsis: A spoken-word number from a card deck about the psychology of professional wrestling. It is performed by a toy wrestling figure inside its toy box, for whoever happens to be there.
bestOfReason: Heads 1-4: babyface, heel, tweener and the head from the package (the jobber).
The trick 9, 13, 14, 11: the box neighbours from the card art teach selling and its lies.
Fear 17, 22: the mask that stays on, the bag nobody opens.
Who decides 45, 46, 49: the spider in a suit, the cricket, the eye on the shelf.
Alone 30, 31: the empty box and the fake crowd on the wall.
Real 35, 55: the cracked head, the cop who writes him up.
Finish 41, 42, 56 + the jobber's choice (4, second beat).

omitted.5-8: big-body archetypes repeat the roster joke
omitted.23-29: cut for length; 29 overlaps the tweener
omitted.32-34: plant, shooter, sandbag cut so 35 carries 'real'

orderReason: Deck order kept except: the oversell clown 11 comes after the stomp punch as the overdone counterexample; the jobber's power returns as the final card beat.

songLineChanges.songLine: kicking out at two point nine nine, crowd vertical

cues.cue: plastic click at every head swap

beats: Lid's open. A kid is back, or you are, or nobody is and the box just creaked. I perform anyway. I'm plastic. Performing is the whole job.
Big Bad Brain Wrestling, it says on the lid. One body, four heads, a cardboard ring. Every head is somebody else, and every one of them swears the fight is real.

beats.pre: Click. Golden head.
beats.text: The Babyface: high-flying moves, because audiences cheer for that. A slave to approval.

beats.pre: Click. Sneer head.
beats.text: The Heel: brutal, sneaky moves. If they aren't booing, you aren't doing your job.

beats.pre: Click. Sunglasses.
beats.text: The Tweener: the audience decides to cheer for you on their own. You don't ask for it.

beats.pre: And the head that came in the package.
beats.text: The Jobber: isolated and picked apart. You exist to make the other guy look good.

beats: That one is mine. The others are on loan.

beats.pre: My teacher is the opossum by the crayons, staggering from a tiny tap:
beats.text: The Master Seller: maintain the illusion of peril. Limp to the ring. Make them believe.

beats.pre: The kangaroo next to him swears by this one:
beats.text: The Thigh Slap: slapping the thigh when kicking. A loud sound suggests impact. An audio lie.

beats.pre: The donkey answers with a thud:
beats.text: The Stomp Punch: stomping on the mat when punching. Kinetic misdirection.

beats.pre: The chicken overdoes it, every time.
beats.text: The Oversell Clown: reacting to an attack far beyond reality. A mockery of the sport.

beats.pre: The axolotl keeps her mask on, even in the dark.
beats.text: The Sacred Mask: kayfabe sacred to their identity. The biggest identifier. Never remove it.

beats.pre: And there is a canvas bag in the corner nobody opens.
beats.text: The Snake Bag: the bag has a live snake. Terrify them before the match starts.

beats: Who decides how it ends? Look up. Whoever holds the box.

beats.pre: Or the spider in the suit, pulling strings:
beats.text: The Booker: the ending is pre-planned. You are just a puppet.

beats.pre: The cricket calls the next move into my ear.
beats.text: The Spot Caller: calling moves in the ring. A basic outline, filled in with sweat.

beats.pre: And one big eye on the shelf.
beats.text: The Hard Cam: if the camera didn't see it, it didn't happen.

beats.pre: Most nights it's this one.
beats.text: The Empty Arena: taped in empty arenas, pausing for a pop that never comes. Surreal.

beats.pre: So the chameleons on the wall pretend to be a crowd.
beats.text: The Green Screen Crowd: a failed attempt to hide the emptiness. Audio sweetening on a lie.

beats.pre: Then one night a head really cracks.
beats.text: The Real Injury: Goldberg's shoulder smashed into the ring-post. The crowd goes nuts: it's real.

beats.pre: The cop in the corner is writing me up for telling you this.
beats.text: The Kayfabe Police: protecting the business. Keep the secrets secret, or get fired.

beats.pre: Here it comes.
beats.text: The Finisher: the Leg Drop. The most important moment. If this hits, go home.

beats.pre: It hits. And the zebra still kicks out,
beats.text: The False Finish: the art of the near-fall, kicking out at two point nine nine, crowd vertical.

beats.pre: So I lie down the way the phoenix does.
beats.text: The Retirement Match: leaning on the fourth wall. Rising, and falling. See you next season.

beats.pre: One line on the package is still true.
beats.text: When defeated, you may choose who defeats you. That is your only control.

beats: So whoever opened the lid: it's you. You knew the ending and stayed for the near-fall anyway.
Out there they swear it's real. In here it says plastic on the label, and I still give you everything. Close the lid gently. All my heads are in here.
